q.s: A newborn has a single central upper incisor, closely set eyes, a flat single-nostril nose and a cleft lip. She also has polydactyly and a heart defect. Brain MRI shows a single fused ventricle with no separation of the cerebral hemispheres.
o: Division of the prosencephalon into two hemispheres, often from Sonic hedgehog defects
e: Correct. Holoprosencephaly, seen in Patau syndrome.
q.ch: Midline facial defects + trisomy 13 features + single ventricle → holoprosencephaly → failed prosencephalon division (SHH).
q.tr: Fetal alcohol syndrome can also cause holoprosencephaly.
q.q2: Failure of which process caused the brain malformation?

q.s: A 45-year-old woman has a slowly growing mass at the base of her skull. She now has hoarseness, difficulty swallowing, loss of the gag reflex on the left and weakness turning her head to the right. Her left shoulder droops.
e: Wrong. CN III, IV, V1, VI.
Correct. CN IX, X and XI.
cl: loss of the gag reflex on the left
weakness turning her head to the right
q.ch: CN IX + X + XI deficits together → jugular foramen syndrome (e.g., glomus tumor).
q.tr: Tongue deviation would add the hypoglossal canal.
q.q2: Through which opening do the affected nerves exit?

q.s: A 30-year-old man had surgery for a suprasellar tumor. Afterward, he eats constantly and has gained 15 kg in 3 months. He also has outbursts of rage.
e: Correct. Satiety center stimulated by leptin.
q.ch: Hypothalamic damage + hyperphagia + rage → ventromedial nucleus (satiety) lesion.
q.tr: "If you zap your ventromedial nucleus, you grow ventrally and medially."
q.q2: Damage to which hypothalamic nucleus explains his eating?

q.s: A 23-year-old man was stabbed in the back with a knife. His neurologic exam is shown.
o: Left hemisection of the spinal cord at T10
Right hemisection of the cord at T10
cl: stabbed in the back with a knife
q.ch: Ipsilateral UMN weakness and dorsal column loss + contralateral pain/temperature loss 1–2 levels below → hemisection → Brown-Séquard.
q.tr: Spinothalamic fibers cross at the anterior white commissure 1–2 segments above entry.

q.s: A 70-year-old man has an open repair of a thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm. When he wakes, he cannot move his legs and cannot feel pinprick below the umbilicus. He can still feel a tuning fork on his toes and knows which way his toes are moved.
o: Anterior spinal artery, via the artery of Adamkiewicz
cl: cannot feel pinprick below the umbilicus
can still feel a tuning fork
q.ch: Aortic surgery + paraplegia + pain loss with spared vibration/proprioception → anterior spinal artery infarct.
q.tr: The artery of Adamkiewicz supplies the anterior cord below about T8.

q.s: A 62-year-old woman has tingling in her feet and is unsteady in the dark. She has lost vibration and position sense in her toes, her legs are spastic with brisk knee reflexes and her plantar responses are extensor. Her laboratory results are shown.
o: Dorsal columns, lateral corticospinal tracts and spinocerebellar tracts
e: Correct. Subacute combined degeneration from B12 deficiency.
q.ch: Pernicious anemia (anti-IF, ↑ MMA) + dorsal column loss + UMN signs → subacute combined degeneration.
q.tr: Folate deficiency raises homocysteine but not methylmalonic acid.
q.q2: Which spinal cord tracts are affected?

q.s: A 4-month-old girl has never been able to hold up her head. She is profoundly floppy, with absent reflexes and fine twitching of her tongue. She follows faces with her eyes and smiles.
cl: follows faces with her eyes and smiles
q.ch: Infant hypotonia + areflexia + tongue fasciculations + normal cognition → SMA type 1 → anterior horn cells.
q.tr: Autosomal recessive SMN1 defect; "floppy baby."

q.s: A 66-year-old woman with poorly controlled hypertension suddenly develops a severe headache and weakness of her left arm and leg, then becomes drowsy. CT shows a large hemorrhage in the right basal ganglia.
o: Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysm of a lenticulostriate artery
Arteriovenous malformation of the occipital lobe
cl: weakness of her left arm and leg
hemorrhage in the right basal ganglia
q.ch: Chronic hypertension + basal ganglia hemorrhage → Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms of lenticulostriate arteries.
q.tr: Lobar bleeds in older normotensive adults suggest amyloid angiopathy.
q.q2: Which vascular lesion caused the bleed?

q.s: An 84-year-old man who takes warfarin has become increasingly confused and sleepy over 3 weeks. He fell at home a month ago but did not hit his head hard. CT shows a crescent-shaped dark collection over the left hemisphere that crosses suture lines.
o: Bridging veins between the cortex and dural sinuses
cl: increasingly confused and sleepy over 3 weeks
q.ch: Elderly + anticoagulation + minor fall + gradual confusion + hypodense crescent → chronic subdural → bridging veins.
q.tr: Brain atrophy stretches bridging veins.

head: CSF finding
Result
Reference
rows: Present in CSF, absent in serum

q.s: A 26-year-old woman has numbness that started in her right leg and spread over a week. A year ago, she had blurry vision in her left eye that hurt when she moved it and resolved. MRI shows several white matter lesions next to the lateral ventricles. Her results are shown. She is started on natalizumab.
o: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy from JC virus
cl: hurt when she moved it and resolved
q.ch: MS (dissemination in time and space + oligoclonal bands) → natalizumab → risk of PML from JC virus.
q.tr: Check JC virus antibody status before and during natalizumab.
q.q2: Which complication must she be monitored for?

q.s: A 68-year-old woman has sudden weakness of her right leg and foot. Her right arm is only mildly weak, and her face is normal. She is also less spontaneous and has urinary incontinence.
e: Correct. Medial motor and sensory cortex for the leg.
cl: weakness of her right leg and foot
q.ch: Contralateral leg > arm weakness + incontinence + abulia → ACA stroke.
q.tr: The homunculus places the leg on the medial surface.

q.s: A 60-year-old man has right facial paralysis including his forehead, reduced tear production and taste on the right, vertigo, right-sided hearing loss and ringing, and loss of pain and temperature on the left side of his body. He also has right limb ataxia.
e: Correct. Lateral pontine syndrome; labyrinthine artery causes deafness.
Wrong. No facial nucleus or hearing loss.
cl: right facial paralysis including his forehead
q.ch: LMN facial palsy + ipsilateral deafness + contralateral pain loss + ipsilateral ataxia → lateral pons → AICA.
q.tr: "Facial droop means AICA's pooped."

q.s: A 66-year-old man suddenly cannot open his left eye. When the lid is lifted, the eye points down and out and the pupil is dilated. His right arm and leg are weak.
e: Correct. CN III fascicles and cerebral peduncle.
cl: points down and out and the pupil is dilated
His right arm and leg are weak
suddenly cannot open his left eye
q.ch: Ipsilateral CN III palsy + contralateral hemiplegia → ventral midbrain → Weber syndrome (PCA branches).
q.tr: Crossed signs localize to the brainstem.

q.s: A 31-year-old man recovers from HSV encephalitis. He now cannot form new memories, places nonfood objects in his mouth, eats excessively and makes inappropriate sexual advances.
o: Amygdalae and hippocampi in the temporal lobes
cl: places nonfood objects in his mouth
q.ch: HSV encephalitis → bilateral temporal damage → amygdalae (Klüver-Bucy) + hippocampi (anterograde amnesia).
q.tr: HSV-1 encephalitis favors the temporal lobes.

q.s: A 48-year-old woman has a shaky voice and tremor of both hands when she lifts a cup or writes. The tremor disappears when her hands rest in her lap and improves after a glass of wine. Her mother had the same problem.
e: Correct. Essential tremor; primidone is an alternative.
cl: when she lifts a cup or writes
improves after a glass of wine
Her mother had the same problem
q.ch: Bilateral action tremor + alcohol response + family history → essential tremor → propranolol.
q.tr: Parkinson tremor is worse at rest.

q.s: A 41-year-old woman has an uncomfortable crawling sensation in her legs every evening that forces her to get up and walk, which relieves it. Her husband says her legs jerk during sleep. She has heavy periods.
e: Correct. Restless legs syndrome is associated with iron deficiency.
cl: crawling sensation in her legs every evening
q.ch: Evening leg discomfort relieved by movement + menorrhagia → restless legs syndrome → check iron stores.
q.tr: Also associated with CKD and diabetes; treat with dopamine agonists or gabapentinoids.
q.q2: Which test should be checked first?
q.fc: Family pedigree; shaded individuals have café-au-lait macules

q.s: A 7-year-old boy has eight light-brown flat skin patches larger than 5 mm, freckles in his armpits and small pigmented spots on his irises. Several family members are affected, as shown.
o: Regulation of cell-cell adhesion through merlin
cl: small pigmented spots on his irises
q.ch: Café-au-lait spots + axillary freckling + Lisch nodules + autosomal dominant pedigree → NF1 → neurofibromin (RAS GAP).
q.tr: Watch for optic gliomas and pheochromocytoma.
q.q2: What is the normal function of the defective gene's product?

q.s: A 35-year-old man has headaches and unsteadiness. MRI shows a cystic mass in the right cerebellar hemisphere. Abdominal CT shows bilateral kidney masses and cysts. His hemoglobin is 18.5 g/dL. His father died of kidney cancer.
cl: cystic mass in the right cerebellar hemisphere
His father died of kidney cancer
q.ch: Cerebellar hemangioblastoma + bilateral RCC + polycythemia + family history → VHL (chromosome 3).
q.tr: "VHL = 3 letters = chromosome 3."
q.q2: On which chromosome is the defective gene?

q.s: An infant has a dark red, flat birthmark over her right forehead and upper eyelid. At 6 months she has focal seizures involving her left side. Skull imaging shows "tram-track" calcifications in the right hemisphere.
cl: dark red, flat birthmark over her right forehead
focal seizures involving her left side
q.ch: V1 port-wine stain + seizures + ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma → Sturge-Weber → somatic GNAQ mutation.
q.tr: Also early-onset glaucoma.

head: Test
Result
Reference
rows: 2.1-cm sellar mass touching the optic chiasm

q.s: A 29-year-old woman has not had a period for 8 months and has a milky discharge from both breasts. She has started bumping into doorframes. Her results are shown.
cl: not had a period for 8 months
q.ch: Amenorrhea + galactorrhea + high prolactin + macroadenoma at chiasm → prolactinoma → cabergoline.
q.tr: Prolactin inhibits GnRH, causing amenorrhea.

q.s: A 55-year-old woman has a seizure. MRI shows a round, enhancing mass attached to the dura over the left frontal convexity, with a thin "tail" of enhancing dura. Surgical pathology shows cells in whorls and round laminated calcifications.
e: Correct. Psammoma bodies; arachnoid cell origin.
q.ch: Dural-based mass with tail + whorls + psammoma bodies → meningioma.
q.tr: Often found incidentally; more common in women.

q.s: An 18-year-old has trouble seeing at night and keeps bumping into things on either side. As a child he had fatty diarrhea. His blood smear shows red cells with spiky projections. Fundoscopy shows bone spicule–shaped pigment in the peripheral retina.
cl: bumping into things on either side
q.ch: Night blindness + peripheral loss + malabsorption + acanthocytes + bone spicules → retinitis pigmentosa with abetalipoproteinemia.
q.tr: Abetalipoproteinemia is an MTP deficiency with fat-soluble vitamin loss.
q.q2: Which retinal disorder does he have?

q.s: A 52-year-old man with type 1 diabetes for 30 years has sudden painless loss of vision in his right eye, with many dark floaters. Fundoscopy of the left eye shows fine new vessels growing on the optic disc.
o: Vitreous hemorrhage from fragile new vessels in proliferative retinopathy
cl: new vessels growing on the optic disc
q.ch: Long diabetes + sudden floaters and vision loss + neovascularization → proliferative retinopathy → vitreous hemorrhage.
q.tr: VEGF from retinal hypoxia drives neovascularization; anti-VEGF drugs treat it.
q.fc: Family pedigree; shaded individuals had an eye tumor in childhood

q.s: A 14-month-old boy has a white reflex in his left eye in photographs. Exam shows a white retinal mass in both eyes. His family history is shown.
cl: white reflex in his left eye
white retinal mass in both eyes
q.ch: Bilateral retinoblastoma + affected relatives → germline RB1 loss (two-hit) → later osteosarcoma.
q.tr: Inherited as autosomal dominant though the gene acts recessively at the cell level.
q.q2: Which tumor is this child at increased risk for later in life?

q.s: A 27-year-old man with chronic low back stiffness that improves with exercise has a painful red right eye with sensitivity to light. A thin layer of white cells is settled at the bottom of the front of the eye.
e: Correct. Anterior uveitis with hypopyon in ankylosing spondylitis.
cl: low back stiffness that improves with exercise
settled at the bottom of the front of the eye
q.ch: Inflammatory back pain + painful red eye + hypopyon → anterior uveitis → HLA-B27.
q.tr: Sarcoidosis and Behçet syndrome also cause uveitis.

q.s: A 9-day-old girl born vaginally has swollen eyelids and watery discharge from both eyes. Her mother had no prenatal care. The infant also develops a staccato cough two weeks later.
q.ch: Conjunctivitis at day 5–14 + staccato cough → Chlamydia trachomatis → oral macrolide.
q.tr: Gonococcal conjunctivitis begins at 2–5 days and needs ceftriaxone.

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has painful vision loss in her right eye. When a light is swung from her left eye to her right eye, both pupils dilate. When the light is moved back to the left eye, both pupils constrict.
e: Wrong. Efferent; right pupil would not constrict at all.
Correct. Relative afferent pupillary defect from optic neuritis.
cl: painful vision loss in her right eye
swung from her left eye to her right eye, both pupils dilate
Weak afferent input on the right.
q.ch: Swinging-flashlight dilation in the right eye → right afferent (optic nerve) lesion → Marcus Gunn pupil.
q.tr: Both pupils always stay equal in size with a pure afferent lesion.
q.q2: Which part of the reflex pathway is damaged?

q.s: A 24-year-old man was punched in the left eye. He has double vision when he looks up, his left eye appears sunken and his left cheek and upper lip are numb.
cl: double vision when he looks up
his left cheek and upper lip are numb
q.ch: Blunt eye trauma + diplopia on upgaze + enophthalmos + cheek numbness → orbital floor fracture → inferior rectus entrapment.
q.tr: In children, a "white-eyed" trapdoor fracture can trigger the oculocardiac reflex.

q.s: After a fall from a bicycle, a 16-year-old has double vision that is worse when he walks downstairs or reads. His right eye sits higher than the left. He tilts his head toward his left shoulder to make the double vision go away.
e: Wrong. Down and out with ptosis.
cl: worse when he walks downstairs or reads
His right eye sits higher than the left
tilts his head toward his left shoulder
q.ch: Vertical diplopia on downgaze + right hypertropia + head tilt to left → right CN IV palsy.
q.tr: CN IV is the thinnest and longest intracranial nerve, often injured by trauma.

q.s: A 40-year-old woman with recurrent ear infections has had foul-smelling drainage from her right ear for months without pain. Her hearing on the right has worsened. Otoscopy shows a pearly white mass behind a retracted eardrum.
o: Conductive; ear canal occlusion by wax
Conductive; erosion of the ossicles by keratinized squamous epithelium
cl: foul-smelling drainage from her right ear for months without pain
q.ch: Painless chronic otorrhea + pearly white retrotympanic mass → cholesteatoma → ossicular erosion → conductive loss.
q.tr: "Skin in the wrong place."
q.q2: What is the type of hearing loss and its mechanism?
q.fc: Pure-tone audiogram (air and bone conduction equal)

q.s: A 74-year-old man says that people mumble and that he cannot follow conversations in restaurants. He has no ear pain or vertigo. Otoscopy is normal. His audiogram is shown.
o: Age-related loss of hair cells at the base of the cochlea
Loss of hair cells at the cochlear apex
q.ch: Elderly + bilateral symmetric high-frequency sensorineural loss → presbycusis → basal cochlear hair cell loss.
q.tr: High frequencies are heard at the stiff, narrow base.
q.q2: What is the cause of his hearing loss?

q.s: A 44-year-old woman has episodes of severe spinning lasting 2–4 hours, with nausea. Before each attack her left ear feels full, and she has a roaring sound in it. Over time, hearing in her left ear has worsened for low tones.
o: Viral inflammation of the vestibular nerve
Increased endolymph volume in the inner ear
q.ch: Episodic vertigo for hours + aural fullness + tinnitus + fluctuating sensorineural loss → Ménière → endolymphatic hydrops.
q.tr: "Men wear vests": vertigo, sensorineural loss, tinnitus.

q.s: A 40-year-old man with 35% body surface area burns 10 days ago needs surgery. After induction with succinylcholine, his ECG shows tall peaked T waves followed by a wide-complex rhythm.
o: Release of potassium from muscle with upregulated extrajunctional nicotinic receptors
cl: 35% body surface area burns 10 days ago
q.ch: Burns (or crush, denervation) + succinylcholine → depolarization of upregulated receptors → K+ efflux → hyperkalemia → arrhythmia.
q.tr: Use a nondepolarizing agent such as rocuronium instead.

q.s: A 70-year-old man in septic shock with a BP of 78/40 mm Hg needs urgent intubation. The team chooses an induction agent that keeps his blood pressure stable. The next day he remains hypotensive despite fluids, and a random cortisol is low.
e: Wrong. Raises BP; no adrenal effect.
q.ch: Hemodynamically neutral induction + later low cortisol → etomidate → adrenal insufficiency.
q.tr: Ketamine raises BP and HR; propofol drops BP.
q.fc: CNS depression at increasing doses of two sedatives

q.s: Two sedative-hypnotics that both act on the GABA-A receptor are compared as shown. Drug P plateaus because it only enhances the effect of GABA that is already present.
o: Its overdose is reversed by flumazenil
It is safe in acute porphyria
It increases the duration of chloride channel opening and can directly open the channel at high doses
It increases the frequency of chloride channel opening
It has no effect on respiration
cl: both act on the GABA-A receptor
only enhances the effect of GABA that is already present
q.ch: Ceiling effect = benzodiazepine (↑ frequency); no ceiling = barbiturate (↑ duration, direct opening) → coma and death.
q.tr: "Frenzodiazepines" ↑ frequency; "barbidurates" ↑ duration.
q.q2: Which statement about drug Q is correct?

q.s: A 67-year-old woman with Parkinson disease has stretches each day when her levodopa wears off before the next dose. A drug is added that blocks dopamine breakdown in the brain without affecting peripheral L-DOPA metabolism.
cl: wears off before the next dose
blocks dopamine breakdown in the brain
q.ch: Wearing-off + central dopamine breakdown blocker → MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline, rasagiline).
q.tr: Tolcapone also blocks central COMT but is hepatotoxic.

q.s: A 28-year-old woman with bipolar disorder and epilepsy was started on a new drug 3 weeks ago. Her dose was increased quickly because she was also taking valproate. She now has fever, painful mouth ulcers and a widespread rash with skin peeling.
e: Correct. SJS risk increases with rapid titration and valproate co-therapy.
cl: increased quickly because she was also taking valproate
q.ch: Mood stabilizer + anticonvulsant + rapid titration with valproate + mucocutaneous blistering → lamotrigine SJS.
q.tr: Phenytoin and carbamazepine also cause SJS.

q.s: A 5-year-old girl has a tonsillectomy and is given codeine for pain. That night she is very sleepy, her pupils are pinpoint and she is breathing slowly. Her mother had a similar reaction after a dental procedure.
o: Ultrarapid CYP2D6 metabolism converting codeine to morphine
cl: her pupils are pinpoint and she is breathing slowly
Her mother had a similar reaction
q.ch: Codeine prodrug + toxicity in child and parent → ultrarapid CYP2D6 metabolism → excess morphine.
q.tr: Poor metabolizers get no pain relief from codeine.

q.s: A 58-year-old man with chronic knee pain who takes sertraline is started on a pain reliever. A week later he is agitated and sweating, with tremor, diarrhea and jerking muscles. His temperature is 39°C, and reflexes are brisk with clonus.
e: Correct. Weak opioid that inhibits serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake.
Wrong. Does not inhibit serotonin reuptake.
cl: agitated and sweating, with tremor, diarrhea
q.ch: SSRI + tramadol → serotonin syndrome (autonomic, mental status, clonus).
q.tr: Tramadol also lowers seizure threshold.

q.s: A 70-year-old woman with open-angle glaucoma uses eye drops every night. Over months, her treated green eye turns brown, and her eyelashes on that side grow longer and darker.
o: Contracts the ciliary muscle to open the trabecular meshwork
Decreases aqueous production via α2 agonism
Increases uveoscleral outflow as a prostaglandin F2α analog
Dilates the pupil via α1 agonism
Decreases aqueous production by inhibiting carbonic anhydrase
cl: her treated green eye turns brown
eyelashes on that side grow longer and darker
q.ch: Glaucoma drop + iris browning + eyelash growth → latanoprost → ↑ uveoscleral outflow.
q.tr: β-blockers and acetazolamide cause no pupil or vision change.
q.q2: How does her drug lower intraocular pressure?
